topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: That tree, the one I planted with my own hands, sapling as I was, just a sprout of a lad, it's gone now. Gone, just like the day's light when the sun sets. They say it was in the way, an obstacle for progress. Progress, they call it. But it was part of me, that tree, rooted in my childhood, shading my memories. Now it's just a stump, a scar in the earth. I can almost hear the echo of the axe, each swing a slice through the years. What good is a field clear of obstacles if it’s clear of all that's dear, too? The saints know, I did my best by that tree. I watered it when the rains failed, I whispered to it, told it secrets. But no one listens to a farmer, not even the saints it seems.
